scope: Reduce repeated simplex-gradient construction in clumpy belt dust; preserve the spatial noise, raymarch integration, depth clipping and optics.

implementation.texture: 289x289 RGBA32F, nearest, repeat S/T, no mipmaps. Texel(x,y)=gradient(permute(permute(y)+x)). CPU float-rounded gradients; GPU retains z permutation and unchanged simplex kernel.
implementation.ownership: One texture per clumpy RingDustRaymarchMaterial; none for unclumped rings. Copy adopts the uniform clone, dispose releases the uploaded texture and retains ownership for subsequent reuse.
implementation.memory: 1,336,336 bytes of texel data on GPU plus a retained CPU array of the same size per material. No 3D field approximation or GPU baking.
implementation.preservation: Both octaves, clump strength/scale, march steps, jitter, depth clipping and other lighting/opacity calculations unchanged. Shared Noise.ts and CPU terrain noise unchanged.

method.gpu: AMD Radeon Graphics / ANGLE D3D11, native Chrome 155, 1280x720 DPR 1
method.assets: Real Alkaid and W26 resources from Yandex S3, Vite dev server
method.frozenInputs: Stop engine; capture actual dust uniforms, camera and world transform; preserve profile textures; copy scene depth to a private Float render target.
method.reference: Original RingDustRaymarchMaterial.ts extracted from commit 012c56a2. Enable the same clump/phase/arcs/light/extinction options and use the actual volume defines and uniforms for both programs.
method.rendering: Actual dust proxy, NoBlending RGBA32F output; six warmups and 32 native GPU elapsed queries per variant. Baseline and production repeated in the same capture.
method.image: All raw HDR RGBA components compared before blending/postprocessing, relative L1=sum(abs(error))/sum(abs(reference)); alpha coverage also checked.
method.limits: Two frozen views, one native GPU. These are isolated dust draw timings, not total frame times or production build performance. Screenshots inspected as a sanity check, not proof of image identity.

conclusions.choice: Compact repeat lookup selected. Padded 290x578 table was about 0.4ms faster but used twice the memory. Explicit GLSL wrapping of compact indices was about 0.9ms slower. All layout candidates had the same small float-rounding HDR differences in the measured views.
conclusions.remaining: Audit item 16 stays open: expensive visible geometry/motion and remaining volume costs need further profiling.
